findings.title: Licence is absent from the identity read-list — a faithful migration silently relicenses CC0-1.0 content to CC-BY-4.0
findings.expected: §2.2's principle ('the source wins … report the divergence explicitly and let a human decide; never normalize silently') applied to every identity value the template pre-fills, including license.
findings.observed: The §2.1 identity table has rows only for title, abbreviation, packageId, canonical, version, status/releaseLabel, dependencies, publisher — no license (nor jurisdiction or language). §2.2 names only canonical and packageId. SKILL.md step 2's read-list equally omits license. The source declares license: CC0-1.0 (sushi-config.yaml:17); the module template ships license: CC-BY-4.0 as a LITERAL (template sushi-config.yaml:101), not a {{...}} placeholder, so the step-4 placeholder gate cannot surface it either. There is no detection point at all: the source-wins principle is operationalized solely through the enumerated read-list, and license is never read.
findings.output_excerpt: (no output — zero hits in the entire migration spec)
evidence: mii-kds-module-template sushi-config.yaml:101 (license: CC-BY-4.0, literal not placeholder)
control group: sandbox branch migration/ig-publisher kept license: CC0-1.0 with an explicit 'Modul-Metadaten … unverändert' comment — the previous skill generation preserved it
reproduce: 1. Install mii-ig-migration @ v0.5.2; clone the Dokument module
2. Execute step 2 exactly as written: read the enumerated fields, carry them over
3. Execute spec §5.2: create the skeleton from the template and replace {{...}} placeholders
4. Observe: sushi-config now says CC-BY-4.0; no step flagged it; the canonical /ext/ divergence WAS flagged (§2.2)
findings.proposed_fix: Add license, copyrightYear, jurisdiction and language rows to the §2.1 table (all 'derived — carry over unchanged; changing any is a human decision'). In §2.2, after the canonical/packageId block, add: 'The same applies to every identity value the template pre-fills as a literal — license above all: the template ships license: CC-BY-4.0 as a literal, not a placeholder, so no placeholder check will catch it. Read the source's license and carry it over; relicensing is a human decision, never a default.' Mirror license into SKILL.md step 2's read-list.

findings.title: Two-state target discovery cannot classify a hybrid Simplifier+IG-Publisher module, and 'create the module repository' is both contradictory and ambiguous
findings.expected: Precondition 3 tells me what to do with a module that already carries IG-Publisher scaffolding (ig.ini pointing at another template, _genonce.sh & co., committed docs/ = the live Pages output, committed fsh-generated/) alongside its Simplifier files, and whether migration means a NEW repository or in-place work on a branch.
findings.observed: Precondition 3 offers exactly two states ('already on the template' — keyed on a vendored ig-template/ or an ig.ini template entry pointing at it — and 'not yet'). Dokument matches neither usefully: its ig.ini says template = fhir.base.template#current. Nothing in SKILL.md or the spec mentions .simplifier/, project.yaml, package.bake.yaml, fhir.base.template, or what happens to the pre-existing IG-Publisher files. The Preconditions preamble says 'do not create what is missing' while Precondition 3 says 'create the module repository from …mii-kds-module-template' (the spec correctly defers creation to workflow §5.2 — the imperative leaks into SKILL.md's Preconditions). Precondition 2 defines 'the module repository' as the EXISTING repo, Precondition 3 says to CREATE it, and guardrail 6 / spec §3 presuppose in-place branch work: new-repo-vs-in-place is never resolved (the spec shares the ambiguity). The control group resolved it as in-place, silently.

.claude/skills/mii-ig-migration/SKILL.md:0
.claude/skills/mii-ig-migration/references/migration-spec.md:0
evidence: SKILL.md:34 ('Discover the context. … do not create what is missing.') vs SKILL.md:48-54 (Precondition 3 'create the module repository …')
migration-spec.md:144 (§5.2 'Create the module repository from the template, run its first-run bootstrap')
migration-spec.md:91 (§3 'File write — into a working branch of the target repository') + SKILL.md:165 (guardrail 6)
sandbox: .simplifier/ + project.yaml + implementation-guides/ + package.bake.yaml AND sushi-config.yaml + ig.ini (fhir.base.template#current) + fsh-generated/ + _genonce.sh + committed docs/
reproduce: 1. Run Precondition 3 discovery on the Dokument module
2. Observe the module is 'not yet on the template' only by elimination; nothing addresses the existing IG-Publisher half

findings.proposed_fix: In Precondition 3, replace the create-imperative with pure discovery (three states: on-template / plain-Simplifier / hybrid-or-other-template), instruct for the hybrid state: 'inventory the pre-existing IG-Publisher files and record in the migration report which are replaced by the template (ig.ini, _gen*/_update* scripts), which are retired (Simplifier project files after Gate D), and which carry content (fsh-generated/, docs/)'. Move the creation action into the numbered Procedure (see F-14) and state explicitly there whether it means a new repository or vendoring the template into a working branch of the existing one, and who decides.

findings.title: German-only source vs English-default target: nobody is assigned to produce the English default-language pages
findings.expected: For a source whose entire substantive narrative is German (the normal case for KDS modules), the skill says who produces the English input/pagecontent/*.md — this skill via marked machine translation, fhir-ig-translation, or a human — and how that squares with the 'No fabrication' guardrail.
findings.observed: The Language section covers only (a) the en-default policy and (b) the conditional ^language=de-DE warning (which is live here: input/fsh/common/Meta.fsh:9). Spec §5.4 says 'Move the Manteldokument content into input/pagecontent/*.md' — under en-default that puts German text into the English source position; §5.5 makes German the translation at input/translations/de/. The migration therefore inverts the direction (the German source text becomes the *translation* of English pages that do not yet exist), and no text scopes or assigns that every-page German→English translation. 'Output language follows the target template' (SKILL.md:68-69) implies it without ever stating it. The control group (previous skill generation) avoided the problem by keeping i18n-default-lang: de — the direction reversal is a deliberate template decision, but the migration path for German-only sources was lost with it.
findings.output_excerpt: language: de-DE   (and no i18n-default-lang / i18n-lang anywhere)
evidence: source: 18 German Simplifier .page.md files; input/pagecontent/index.md is unmodified English SUSHI boilerplate ('Feel free to modify this index page…') — not real content
control group: migration/ig-publisher used i18n-default-lang: de with an empty input/translations/en/ scaffold
reproduce: 1. Reach step 4/5 with the Dokument module (German-only narrative)
2. Ask: which language goes into input/pagecontent/*.md? If English — who writes it? If German — the en-default config now labels German text as English
3. Observe neither SKILL.md nor the spec answers
findings.proposed_fix: Add to §Language and spec §5.4: 'When the source narrative is not in the target default language, the migration transfers the source text into input/translations/<source-lang>/pagecontent/ (it is the translation now) and produces the default-language pages as MACHINE TRANSLATIONS of it, every one marked TODO:REVIEW, reviewed at Gate C — this is the one sanctioned exception to No-fabrication, and the source-language text stays the authoritative reference until Gate C signs the English off. fhir-ig-translation's harvest mode covers the resource texts.'

findings.title: fql-scan.sh returns a false green on the actual source — the Definition-of-Done gate is satisfiable with all 130 directives unconverted
findings.expected: A scan of the pre-migration module surfaces its Simplifier/FQL directives (130 in implementation-guides/**/*.page.md), or at least fails loudly when its target set is empty; '--strict exits 0' is trustworthy as the skill's DoD criterion (SKILL.md:203).
findings.observed: Run from the module root, fql-scan.sh scans only input/pagecontent (line 41) → 'No Simplifier or FQL directives found.', exit 0; --strict also exit 0. Passing the directory where the directives actually live uses a non-recursive glob (line 53: for f in "$p"/*.md) → 'No .md target files under: implementation-guides', still exit 0. Only manual file enumeration surfaces the 129/130 findings. Consequence: an agent that skips or half-does the narrative move (pages not yet in input/pagecontent) gets a green --strict, i.e. the skill's own completion gate is vacuously satisfiable. (Post-move, with directives inside input/pagecontent, the scan does work.)
findings.output_excerpt:
== fql-scan (rules: …/fql-rules.tsv) ==

No Simplifier or FQL directives found.
evidence: ig-stats measured 130 directives in the same working tree (analysis-out/mii-ig-dokument-stats.json, directives)
reproduce: 1. cd <Dokument module root> (pre-migration state)
2. $SKILL_DIR/scripts/fql-scan.sh --strict; echo $?
3. Observe exit 0 and 'No … directives found' despite 130 directives in implementation-guides/**
findings.proposed_fix: Make directory arguments recursive (find "$p" -name '*.md'), include implementation-guides/**/*.page.md in the default target set when it exists (pre-migration scans are a documented use), and print the scanned-file count; exit non-zero (or a distinct code) under --strict when the target set is EMPTY, so 'nothing scanned' can never read as 'nothing found'.

findings.title: Two skills' allowed-tools grants cannot execute their own shipped scripts
findings.expected: A skill's allowed-tools covers every command its Procedure instructs running.
findings.observed: mii-ig-migration grants Read Grep Glob WebFetch Bash(sushi:*) Bash(gofsh:*) Bash(git clone/status/diff:*) — no pattern covers scripts/fql-scan.sh, which steps 4 and Verification instruct running (SKILL.md:117, :195). fhir-ig-translation grants only Bash(python3:*), but scripts/ig-translate.sh is #!/usr/bin/env bash. In an unattended/CI run (which SKILL.md:118 recommends for --strict) the skill's core command prompts or fails. fhir-ig-analysis is consistent (Bash(python3:*) covers ig-stats.py). The skill-authoring mechanical checklist cannot catch this — frontmatter-contract.md has no allowed-tools-vs-scripts consistency rule (this run's checklist pass reported all four skills green).

mii-ig-migration/SKILL.md:15:allowed-tools: Read Grep Glob WebFetch Bash(sushi:*) Bash(gofsh:*) Bash(git clone:*) Bash(git status:*) Bash(git diff:*)
fhir-ig-translation/SKILL.md:15:allowed-tools: Read Grep Glob Edit Write Bash(python3:*)

Follow-up: add a rule to skill-authoring's frontmatter contract + checklist — 'every command the body instructs running is covered by allowed-tools; shipped scripts count'.

findings.title: Git-history metrics are computed on shallow clones without detection — bus factor is a constant '100 % → hoch', cadence is fiction
findings.expected: Per the skill's own rule ('A null is not a zero', 'A missing input yields null, never a guess'), git-history metrics on a 1-commit shallow checkout are reported as not derivable.
findings.observed: The tool shallow-clones URL inputs itself (--depth 1) and git_stats() trusts ANY .git without checking .git/shallow — self-cloned and externally supplied shallow checkouts alike. Both reports show 'Bus-Faktor (Wissenskonzentration) | 100 % Top-Autor → hoch' and a Pflege-Kadenz ('10.0 Commits/Jahr') computed from a single commit; the tool's own basis clone has .git/shallow and rev-list count 1. metrics-catalog.md marks these as source 'Git-Historie', mode static, no caveat.
findings.output_excerpt:
analysis-out/_sources/kerndatensatz-basis/.git/shallow
1
evidence: analysis-out/mii-ig-dokument-report.md + mii-ig-base-report.md ('100 % Top-Autor → hoch' in both)
scripts/ig-stats.py (shallow clone for URLs; git_stats without shallow check)
reproduce: 1. python3 ig-stats.py run <any git URL>
2. Read the risk table: bus factor 100 %, cadence from 1 commit
3. Confirm the _sources clone is shallow
findings.proposed_fix: In git_stats(): if .git/shallow exists (or rev-list count == 1 for a URL input the tool cloned), emit null for bus-factor/cadence and render 'nicht ermittelbar (shallow clone)' in the report; optionally offer a --full-history flag that deepens the clone. Add the caveat to metrics-catalog.md.

findings.title: The tool ships the readiness score its own SKILL.md disclaims ('Reifegrad /100', glossed 'Freigabe-Indikator')

The metrics catalog's own disclaimer covers only effort/person-day/schedule forecasts, so catalog and tool are consistent with each other but not with SKILL.md.

findings.title: ig-stats-schema.json is stale against the schemaVersion 1.3 output it claims to describe

The schema's description says 'Ab 1.1' while the tool emits schemaVersion 1.3. findings.title: --validate exits 0 unconditionally — empty, valid and INVALID translation sets are indistinguishable by exit code
findings.expected: Validation failure (any [WARN]) exits non-zero; 'nothing to validate' is distinguishable from 'all valid', so the check is CI-wireable.
findings.observed: exit 0 at line 141 is unconditional in --validate mode: a run WITH [WARN] findings (fail=1, 'Validation: findings present (see [WARN]).') exits 0 exactly like a clean run — and a run against a module with NO input/translations/<lang>/ at all prints '(no directory …)' + 'Validation: no findings.' and also exits 0 (observed on the unmigrated sandbox). The only non-zero exits are usage errors and the not-an-IG-root guard (exit 2). The skill's Verification bullets read as if [OK]/no-[WARN] were a checkable gate.

findings.title: 'Determine the target branch from the repository's own convention' comes with no discovery procedure and no warning for publication-coupled conventions
findings.expected: A short discovery recipe (default branch, PR history, CONTRIBUTING/docs) and a caution when the discovered PR base is itself the publication branch.
findings.observed: Step 8/§5.8 explain only the TEMPLATE's convention (main + branch previews). For this repo the operator had to improvise: default branch master; the only two PRs in history both target master; master is simultaneously the GitHub-Pages source, so merging a conventional PR republishes the live guide. The skill never says how to discover a convention nor that the discovered one can be publication-coupled (mitigated by guardrail 6 and Gate D — the agent never merges — so friction, not defect).

#2 master
#1 master
evidence: production repo: Pages source = master:/docs; 2 PRs, both base master
reproduce: 1. Follow step 8 on a repo that is not on the template
2. Observe there is no instruction for HOW to determine the convention
findings.proposed_fix: Add to step 8: 'Discover the convention from (a) the default branch, (b) the bases of merged PRs, (c) CONTRIBUTING/README. If the conventional PR base is also the publication branch (e.g. Pages served from it), say so in the PR description and at Gate D: merging publishes.'

findings.title: No fallback when the rendered Simplifier IG exists but is not mechanically extractable
findings.expected: Step 1 says what to do when the rendered IG URL is supplied but yields nothing to a non-browser agent (Simplifier project pages and ~guides tabs are client-rendered).
findings.observed: Precondition 1 covers only the missing-URL case (ask and stop). In this run no rendered-guide URL was discoverable by HTTP (project page and ~guides tab render client-side; the repo-recorded guide slug mii-ig-dokument-de 404s under …/guide/<project>/<slug>). The operator improvised the permitted-but-nowhere-instructed fallback: derive the inventory from the repository (implementation-guides/**/toc.yaml) and mark the rendered-IG cross-check TODO:REVIEW. The existing TODO:REVIEW instruction is scoped to directive translation, not inventory extraction.

reproduce: 1. WebFetch the Simplifier project page and its ~guides tab
2. Observe no guide URL is server-rendered
findings.proposed_fix: Add to §5.1: 'If the rendered IG cannot be mechanically extracted, derive the narrative structure from the repository (implementation-guides/**/toc.yaml and *.page.md), mark the rendered-IG cross-check TODO:REVIEW, and have Gate B verify against the rendering by hand.'

findings.title: Skeleton creation has no numbered step in SKILL.md — 'stop before step 3' is ambiguous across the two numbering schemes
findings.expected: SKILL.md's numbered Procedure and the spec's §5 workflow agree on step identity, so Precondition 5's stop point is unambiguous.
findings.observed: Spec §5.2 'Create the skeleton' has no SKILL.md counterpart (Procedure runs 1 inventory, 2 identity, 3 transfer …); the creation action lives only inside Precondition 3. Whether skeleton creation is allowed before Precondition 5's 'stop before step 3' is therefore undecidable from SKILL.md alone. Compounding: placeholder REPLACEMENT (spec §5.2) is weakened to placeholder ACCOUNTING in Precondition 4 — the Procedure never says who writes the identity values into the skeleton; and SKILL.md contains two numbered lists (Preconditions 1-5, Procedure 1-8) so 'step 3' needs qualification anyway.
findings.output_excerpt: Procedure: 1 Inventory / 2 Read identity / 3 Transfer / 4 Migrate narrative / 5 Bilingual / 6 Build+QA / 7 Report / 8 PR — no 'create skeleton'
reproduce: 1. Hit Precondition 5 with a missing toolchain
2. Ask: may I still create the skeleton (spec §5.2)? SKILL.md cannot answer
findings.proposed_fix: Insert 'Create the skeleton (spec §5.2): create/vendor the template, replace every placeholder from the step-2 identity' as Procedure step 3 (renumbering transfer to 4 …), reword Precondition 5 to 'stop before the artefact transfer (spec §5.3)', and keep Precondition 3 discovery-only (see F-02).

findings.title: No precedence rule when sushi-config.yaml and package.json disagree on an identity value — and in this module they do
findings.expected: §2.1 says which file wins when both exist and conflict.
findings.observed: §2.1's 'Absent a sushi-config.yaml, read package.json …' is a fallback order, not a conflict rule. In Dokument, package.json's canonical is …/ext/modul-dokument/ImplementationGuide/mii-ig-dokument (the IG-resource URL) while sushi-config's is …/ext/modul-dokument. The operator used sushi-config's value and flagged the disagreement; the spec never instructs either.
findings.output_excerpt: https://www.medizininformatik-initiative.de/fhir/ext/modul-dokument/ImplementationGuide/mii-ig-dokument
evidence: source sushi-config.yaml canonical vs package.json canonical
reproduce: 1. Read both files' canonical
2. Search §2.1/§2.2 for a conflict rule
findings.proposed_fix: Add to §2.1: 'When both files exist and disagree, sushi-config.yaml wins (it is what the build reads); record the disagreement in the migration report.'

findings.title: The script never cross-checks <lang> against the guide's i18n configuration — a deliberate delegation, but unstated risk residue
findings.expected: Given Preconditions 2 calls the language pair 'the step that must not be skipped', the tool could warn when <lang> is not among parameters.i18n-lang or when i18n-default-lang is undeclared.
findings.observed: The script (by documented design: header comment lines 16-18, missing-arg error lines 44-48) only enforces that SOME language is explicitly passed; it never reads sushi-config.yaml's i18n parameters. --scan de on this guide — which declares neither parameter and whose narrative IS German — proceeds without a flag, mechanically proposing German-as-translation-of-German targets. The same holds for --validate. Precondition-2 enforcement rests entirely on the agent reading SKILL.md prose.
findings.output_excerpt: hits only in comments/error text instructing the CALLER to derive <lang>; no config read
reproduce: 1. Run --scan de on a guide with no i18n parameters
2. Observe no warning
findings.proposed_fix: Best-effort warning (not a failure): if sushi-config.yaml is readable and <lang> is absent from parameters.i18n-lang (or i18n-default-lang is undeclared), print 'WARN: <lang> is not a configured target language — see SKILL.md Preconditions 2'.

findings.title: Harvest mode — the realistic path for this module — has an English-only page_map example and went unexercised in this run
findings.expected: The harvest config's example anticipates non-English source page names, since harvesting an existing German rendering is exactly the KDS-module scenario.
findings.observed: harvest-config.yaml's page_map example uses English page names; the Dokument module's pages are German (Beschreibung, Kontext-Bezuege, Referenzen …). The module genuinely carries the harvest machinery the config names (resources.source_kind: fsh-translation-extensions — a Translation RuleSet writing the hl7 translation extension exists at input/fsh/common/rulesets.fsh:46-51; the analysis output flagged i18n.fsh_translation_ext: true). The config's own warning that a wrong page_map entry is 'silently harvested into a file nothing renders' (line 36) is untested against German names. NOTE: this run validated the skill's refusal path but exercised zero percent of harvest mode — see the README's not-done list; this finding records only what is readable from the files.
findings.output_excerpt: harvest-config.yaml:36 (silent-mismap warning), :53-61 (fsh-translation-extensions)
reproduce: 1. Read harvest-config.yaml's page_map example
2. Compare with the module's German page names
findings.proposed_fix: Extend the page_map example with a German→target mapping (e.g. 'Beschreibung.page.md: guidance.md') and one sentence on naming: keys are the SOURCE rendering's page identifiers, whatever their language.

findings.title: package.json's canonical is the IG-resource URL, not the canonical base — it disagrees with sushi-config.yaml
findings.expected: package.json canonical == sushi-config canonical (…/fhir/ext/modul-dokument).
findings.observed: package.json: …/fhir/ext/modul-dokument/ImplementationGuide/mii-ig-dokument. A migration reading identity from package.json (the spec's fallback path) would carry a wrong canonical. For the module's maintainers to assess — NOT changed by this dry run (production is untouchable here).
findings.output_excerpt: https://www.medizininformatik-initiative.de/fhir/ext/modul-dokument/ImplementationGuide/mii-ig-dokument
reproduce: 1. Read both files at master@9f76fed8
findings.proposed_fix: Module maintainers: align package.json canonical with the sushi-config canonical base (report-only from this dry run).

findings.title: '43 files under input/fsh/' does not reproduce — the tree has 34 files (28 .fsh); 43 is the ALIAS count
findings.expected: §2.1's stated counts reproduce on master@9f76fed8.
findings.observed: find input/fsh -type f → 34 (28 .fsh + 3 .gitkeep + 3 example attachments). The FSH sources declare exactly 43 Alias: entries — almost certainly the number that was miscounted. '19 generated resources' is correct.
findings.command: find input/fsh -type f | wc -l; grep -rhE '^Alias\s*:' input/fsh --include='*.fsh' | wc -l
findings.output_excerpt: 34 files; 43 aliases
reproduce: 1. Run the two commands above from the module root
findings.proposed_fix: Correct §2.1 to '34 files (28 .fsh) under input/fsh/, 43 FSH aliases, 19 generated resources'.
